I farm this millet plot every year like my father did. Last season the rains were not too bad, so I harvested enough to feed my family and sell a little. I will buy one bag of NPK when the agro-dealer brings it to our market — one bag is about what I can manage for this small plot, and I will put some old cow manure from my kraal on the weaker patches. I plant my own saved millet seed with cowpea in between the rows, like always, and my sons and I will do most of the work ourselves, though I will pay two or three young men to help at weeding time when the grass grows fast.
